Apply typography styles

Use the appropriate typography style for all the text in your component and in your design overall.

Apply dimensions to your component

Apply dimension tokens to each part of your component, using the ‘Spacing’ and ‘Radius’ tokens from the foundation library.



warning  Best practice
When to use ‘0’ value tokens

Use the ‘0’ raw value when the value is not meant to change within a given context.


If the component is scalable and the value is meant to change, use the ‘0’ value token.


For example, in the ‘Flyout menu’ component, the space between options is set using a raw value ‘0’ since there won’t be a need for the space to change across brands or products.



savings  Mandatory rule
Set minimum tappable area

Set a minimum tappable area of 48x48px for interactive components with dimensions below 48px in either or both directions.


The minimum tappable area is required for good accessibility.



Create a frame with dimensions of 48x48px - use the ‘minimum-tappable-area’ token from the ‘sizing’ category for these numbers.
Create the component inside that frame.

savings  Mandatory rule
How to use the vertical and horizontal resizing options

Fixed width resizing

If you want a component to always be ‘Fixed’, then set it as ‘Fixed’.


Components with text inside them should never have ‘Fixed’ height as this creates accessibility issues if a user enlarges the text by 400%



‘Hug contents’ resizing

If you want a component to always be ‘Hug’, then set it as ‘Hug’.


For example, in the ‘Tag’ component we want the width of the component to change based on the copy so the width is set to ‘hug’, where as the height needs to remain the same so it is set to ‘Fixed’.



"Fill" container resizing.

If you want a component to always be ‘Fill’,then set is as ‘Fill’.



‘Fill container’ or ‘Hug contents’ resizing

If you want a component to sometimes be "Fill" and other times "Hug", initially set it as "Hug" and then change it accordingly in the design.



Component dimension resizing edits

The above rules apply to the component as a whole. When it comes to individual component parts, you should only make edits within the component set and NEVER modify them directly in your design. This ensures that the code generator plugin can accurately reproduce the component instances.

How to apply border correctly

If your component includes a border, always ensure it is set on the inside.


Advance auto-layout settings for Web Components

When applying a border to a web component, make sure to always select the Strokes to be included in your Auto-layout settings.



Advance auto-layout settings for Mobile Components

When applying a border to a mobile component, make sure to always select the Strokes to be excluded in your Auto-layout settings.


warning  Best practice
How to insert images

Static, mood image

If your component contains a bespoke, static, mood image, insert the image using a colour fill.


Content image

If your component contains a content, dynamic image, for example, in the case of an avatar or image used as an information carrier, insert the image by dragging and dropping.
